question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+x-2}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{(x+2)(x-1)}{(x+1)(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{(x+2)\cancel{(x-1)}}{(x+1)\cancel{(x-1)}} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

We then can compute the limit at $x=1,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{x+2}{x+1} \\  & =\frac{1+2}{1+1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}g(1) & ={lim}_{x\to 1}g(x) \\ b & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, for the function to be continuous at $x=1,$ we need $b=\frac{3}{2}.$
